name: Ziyarid dynasty
alt: Ziyarid state of Gilan and Tabaristan

predecessors.name: Asfar Ibn Shiruya
predecessors.text: Asfar's former territories, 'which included Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan, Abhar, Qom and Karaj'

predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Hamadan, Dinavar, Kashan and Isfahan, the 'Abbasid cities' Mardavij captured after 931, and Ahvaz (Khuzestan) by 934

successors.name: Nizari Ismaili state
successors.text: Tabaristan, Gilan and Gorgan, 'invaded and conquered' in 1090

ledger.x: 931: Mardavij founds the Ziyarid state at Isfahan.
931: Mardavij takes the Abbasid cities of the Jibal.
931: Mardavij defeats and kills Asfar and takes his lands.
932: Mardavij conquers Tabaristan.
932: Gurgan passes to Mardavij with Tabaristan (inference).
933: Mardavij cedes Gurgan to the Samanids.
934: Mardavij's troops reach Ahvaz.
934: Ali ibn Buya in Shiraz acknowledges Mardavij.
935: the Buyids take Mardavij's central and southern possessions.
935: Mardavij's death ends the Buyid acknowledgement.

c. 935: Vushmgir takes Gorgan from the Samanids. The Ziyarid page says he, crowned in Ray, 'then wrested Gorgan from Samanid control' (no year); it follows the accession of 935 and precedes the turn-over to Makan in 936.
935: Vushmgir rules from Ray.
936: Vushmgir turns Gorgan over to Makan.
938: Vushmgir retakes Isfahan.
940: the Buyid Hasan retakes Isfahan from Vushmgir ('retook Isfahan in 940').
943: Ray is lost to the Buyids.

943: the capital is Gorgan (infobox 'Gorgan (943-1035)'); the narrative has Makan, al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan and the Buyids holding Gorgan in 936-947 and 948-954, so the infobox date is the page's and the residence is not borne out.

c. 944: al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan defeats Vushmgir in Tabaristan. After Ray was lost in 943, 'Returning to Tabaristan, he was defeated there by al-Hasan, who had previously occupied Gorgan'; Vushmgir fled to the Bavandids and then to the Samanid court (no year on these sentences: placed between 943 and 945). Al-Hasan…
945: Vushmgir's campaign for Gorgan begins.
947: Vushmgir takes Gorgan and Tabaristan from al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan.
947: the contest with al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan ends with his expulsion from Tabaristan and Gorgan.
948: the Buyid Hasan takes Tabaristan and Gorgan.
948: the Buyid invasion begins a struggle for Tabaristan and Gorgan.
955: a Samanid-brokered treaty ends the first round.
955: Vushmgir holds Tabaristan and Gorgan again.
958: Vushmgir briefly occupies Ray ('briefly occupied Ray').
958: the occupation of Ray ends in the same year (assumed).
960: Rukn al-Dawla's counterattacks begin.
966: the last Buyid counterattack.
980: the Buyids take Tabaristan.
981: the Buyids take Gorgan ('Gorgan (981)' on the Buyid dynasty page; Qabus's first reign is listed 977-981).
998: Qabus returns.
1035: the capital is Amol.
1090: the Nizari Ismailis end Ziyarid rule.

wars.name: Conquests of Mardavij
wars.outcome: Mardavij killed Asfar (931) and took his lands and the Abbasid cities of the Jibal, conquered Tabaristan (932), made peace with the Samanids in 933 ceding Gurgan, and by 934 was acknowledged as far as Shiraz (Ali ibn Buya, a client) and Ahvaz.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of the Ziyarid south
wars.outcome: After Mardavij's murder in January 935 Ali ibn Buya took his possessions in central and southern Iran and Hasan ibn Buya seized Isfahan; Vushmgir retook Isfahan in 938 and lost it again in 940.

wars.name: Samanid, Buyid and Fairuzanid wars for Ray, Gorgan and Tabaristan
wars.outcome: The Samanid governor Chaghani attacked Gorgan in 939/940 and defeated Vushmgir at Ray; Ray fell to the Buyid Hasan in 943; al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan, Vushmgir's rebel governor of Sari, took Tabaristan and Gorgan and was expelled only in 947 by a Samanid army…

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Tabaristan and Gorgan
wars.outcome: Qabus was expelled in 980 and fled to Khorasan; the Buyids held Tabaristan (980) and Gorgan (981) until he returned in 998.

wars.name: Ghaznavid and Seljuq overlordship
wars.outcome: Manuchihr 'quickly recognized the sovereignty of Mahmud of Ghazni' in 1012; in 1035 Abu Kalijar stopped paying tribute and the Ghaznavids sacked Amol; the Seljuqs 'forced him to accept their authority' in 1041/42.

wars.name: Nizari Ismaili conquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: The Nizari Ismaili state invaded and conquered Gilanshah's domains in 1090, ending Ziyarid rule.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded: the Daylam and Tabaristan hill frontiers, the Samanid peace of 933 (Gurgan) and the 955 treaty name regions, not lines; the empty spans 944-946, 948-954 and 980-997 have no frontier.
